messages:
Alex: Customer report: multiple 502/504 gateway errors hitting Hosted API (inference) since ~08:15 UTC. They see a spike in handshake timeouts. Request id samples: r-9a1b, r-9a1c, r-9a1d. Linking logs.
Sofia: @Alex can you paste the curl + error body? curious if this is a backend 5xx or edge TLS fail.
Alex: here's a repro curl from our edge using customer's domain (they're on hosted):

```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.34.12.5) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 300000 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

Body from gateway shows: `502 Gateway Error: upstream handshake timeout (tls: handshake did not complete)`
Devon: I pulled edge traces for r-9a1b — we see resolver resolving to an older CDN origin IP (AS-12345) and the handshake stalls after ClientHello. SNI in the ClientHello is `api.redwood.ai`, server responds nothing. Packet capture snippet: `TLSv1.3 ClientHello, length 512` then nothing.
Priya: Any recent cert rotation? last scheduled cert rotation was 03:00 UTC but completed normally. However I see a partial rollback job for cert chain on some deployers at 07:50 UTC.
Alex: Repro across regions? I see requests failing from us-east-1 and eu-west-1 only; ap-south-1 looks unaffected.
Sofia: Can you run an openssl s_client against the failing IP to see if server replies? ask to run from our jump host in us-east.
Devon: Ran from jump-us-east:

```
openssl s_client -connect 52.34.12.5:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -tlsextdebug -state -msg
# output truncated
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake
>>> ClientHello
# no ServerHello within 10s, connection reset
write:errno=104
```

Priya: That smells like either the origin behind that IP isn't bound to the new cert or there's a middlebox dropping after SNI (SNI-based routing mismatch). Check resolver records TTL and recent CDN origin updates.
Alex: dig +trace for api.redwood.ai from our edge:

```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace api.redwood.ai
;; global options: +cmd
;; Received 1 answer
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN CNAME edge1.cdn.example.net.
edge1.cdn.example.net. 60 IN A 52.34.12.5
edge1.cdn.example.net. 60 IN A 54.210.23.6
```

Sofia: TTL 60 on CDN mapping is low; however some resolvers might have cached older mapping to edge-old.cdn.example.net -> 18.23.45.7 which is on a retired fleet that doesn't have the new cert chain.
Devon: I grabbed the edge-old IP 18.23.45.7 and ran s_client: it responded with an RSA cert that expired yesterday (subject CN api.redwood.ai, not the new ECDSA chain). So we have a partial DNS prop / origin drift.
Priya: Steps: 1) Confirm which origin IPs are advertised by our authoritative DNS pool (control plane). 2) Check edge fleet membership and cert deployment status for those IPs. 3) Add temporary routing rule to avoid edge-old until certs backfilled.
Alex: I opened an emergency support ticket with CDN ops (ticket #CDN-7852) and notified the cert rotation runbook owner. Asking CDN ops to BGP-blackhole 18.23.45.7 from the public pool while we remediate.
Sofia: Quick mitigation for customers: enable fallback to dedicated-hosted route (non-CDN path) for affected customer accounts — can we feature-flag that per-tenant? @Devon?
Devon: We have a per-tenant fallback flag in the console. I can flip it for the 3 affected customers in 5m. That will route them through the origin-gw which has correct cert chain.
Priya: Also recommend increasing DNS TTL temporarily to 300 after we stabilize so caches converge to correct set. Long-term we need a health-check-driven DNS failover instead of manual origin pruning.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-04-2234506789 — severity P2. Owner: Priya. Links: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-04-2234506789
Alex: After CDN ops blackholed 18.23.45.7, errors dropped to baseline in us-east within ~3 minutes. eu-west saw some tailing failures for 8 minutes (resolver caches). Customer updated and reporting normal.
Sofia: Postmortem action items:
- Add origin cert deployment verification step (canaries + mTLS probe) to rotation runbook
- Health-check-based DNS remove/attach policy for CDN origins
- Add automated s_client SNI probes from multiple regions to detect SNI routing mismatches
- Improve observability: surface `tls: handshake did not complete` as a distinct metric in Console
Priya: I'm scheduling a remediation retro with CDN ops and cert team at 13:00 UTC. Will attach logs and the packet capture.

Alex: Thanks all. Leaving the incident open for the retro and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
